column1: # design/dulling-admission.tsv — the new-capability half of the ledger (DESIGN.md A.8). One row
# per way a FUTURE capability can enter the system: what the path admits, what it admits today,
# the requirement that governs the addition, whether it can be added without amending DESIGN.md,
# a verdict, why, and the evidence. Same verdict vocabulary as design/dulling.tsv.
# Columns: path, admits, today, guideline, can_add_without_amending, verdict, why, evidence.

column2: admits
column3: today
column7: why

column1: a new plugin for a genuinely new concept
column2: a plugin serving behaviour that fits no mechanism row
column3: any new concept ships as its own plugin + candy (provide: + its own CUE module)
column7: a capability that fits no row amends a mechanism, here, first — the concept waits on an operator-signed DESIGN.md amendment, where today a plugin needs none

column2: a kind that realizes deployments
column3: kubevirt ships as a seventh substrate in its own plugin (plugin-kubevirt/candy/plugin-kubevirt/charly.yml)
column7: a new kind is a row of _deploymentKind, implemented inside one of the five kind-owning plugins; a standalone kind plugin has no form

column1: a new kind word owned by a third-party plugin
column2: a namespaced node type
column3: plugin-example-kind provides kind: words
column7: the word survives under the plugin's namespace; only the first-party spelling is reserved

column2: an observation a step makes
column3: plugin-wl / plugin-adb provide verb: words; plugin-containerd provides verb:containerd
column7: Nothing else is a first-party verb — a new first-party verb is a row of one of four owners' tables, not a plugin

column1: a new operation on an existing verb
column2: one more choice of an existing verb
column3: wl: / adb: / kube: each expose dozens of operations
column7: an operation is a key of the verb's own input definition, defined in the owning module

column2: a CLI word valid for every kind and driver
column3: plugin-dsh / plugin-strata / plugin-qdrant provide subcommand:
column7: a subcommand role word with its own argument definition, deadline and mutates:

column2: a CLI family for one kind or driver
column3: `charly kubevirt` is a command family of its own today (plugin-kubevirt)
column7: no kind- or driver-specific command groups; a driver is not allowed an interaction path of its own (D-VENUE-1)

column1: a new flag or argument on a command
column2: one more argument of an existing command
column3: every subcommand declares its argument definition
column7: the argument definition is the plugin's; --format json is the one mandated flag

column2: a capability plugins bind
column3: plugin-gpu / plugin-user / plugin-mount provide type: words
column7: a plugin's types are bound through its type role

column2: a service other plugins call
column3: plugin-container provides api:image_load
column7: the api's messages are a tag table in the owner's own CUE module

column2: a new backing tool for an existing subsystem
column3: containerd is an out-of-tree ENGINE PLUGIN providing engine:containerd (plugin-nerdctl/candy/plugin-containerd/charly.yml)
column7: A driver is a row, never a plugin, kind, field or command of its own — an engine can no longer ship as its own plugin

column2: a driver for the agent subsystem
column3: plugin-agent-pi and plugin-tmux are plugins of their own
column7: a runtime is a row of _driver, so a new runtime means contributing to the agent-owning plugin

column2: a leasable host resource
column3: gpu / device / cpu / memory / storage / mount rows
column7: a grant that no host capability type expresses is added as a new type by its plugin

column2: vocabulary data for a distro, init or builder
column3: distro-* and cachyos-pacstrap-builder are data nodes today
column7: a data node is the sanctioned row form (D-PLUG-2)

column2: a step field shared by every verb
column3: retry / stdout / exit_status are per-verb knobs today
column7: Step modifiers are defined once in spec — only spec's owner can add one; a verb cannot carry its own

column2: a comparison applied to a result
column3: matchers today live with each verb's own evaluation
column7: matchers belong to the same spec-owned surface; not, json and one comparison are the whole set

column2: a state a check can observe
column3: today build-time and live states are observed through several contexts (§16.5)
column5: no, row in a closed triple
column7: the phase set is artifact / ready / deployment; each verb declares which it observes, so a new state needs the §16.5 table

column2: a persisted store reached with get/put
column3: content / state / secret / config rows
column7: The host service is closed: adding a method amends this document

column2: one RPC of the host service
column3: venue_exec / get / put / project / call / report / state_commit / audit_append
column7: same closure clause as the store table

column2: a typed plugin service
column3: kind / verb / subcommand / type / api
column7: the role table and the method table are the whole plugin contract, and no sixth role is written in code — a role is added as a row, not by a plugin

column2: a kind of step work
column3: run / check / harness_run / harness_check
column7: the step table has one alternative per intent

column2: what a stage does
column3: steps / another pipeline / deployment checks / ask
column7: A stage does exactly one thing (#StageAlt) — runs steps, runs another pipeline, realizes deployments and runs their checks, or asks the operator

column2: a transport to reach a deployment
column3: container / ssh / shell / kvm / adb / kube; exec / copy / log / console / display / forward / power
column7: every venue is one alternative of #VenueAlt and every access one of the seven; a new transport is a schema arm, not a plugin

column2: a command that edits an authored file
column3: box set / add-candy / rm-candy / write / reconcile, deploy adopt, migrate
column7: only those commands write authored files, each printing what it changed; a new authoring verb must be added to that list

column2: a protocol an endpoint is reached by
column3: endpoint protocol mcp plus publish: (§8.1, D-VAL-13)
column7: wired by the endpoint's protocol (MCP registration for mcp) — each protocol needs its own wiring in the owner

column1: a new check bed (a disposable verification target)
column2: a deployment used as a test target
column3: beds are disposable: true deployments today (TODO.md 3.13 still names beds)
column7: the WORD is retired but the capability is exactly disposable: true plus the artifact/ready/deployment phases — no operation is lost

column1: a new skill or agent definition
column2: authored guidance or a sub-agent
column3: skill: / agent nodes with bodies under .agents/
column7: authoring supplies rows; the skill body path is derived, not declared

column1: a new workflow above the mechanisms
column2: a routine that sequences steps
column3: pipeline / task nodes
column7: pipeline is the one workflow kind ... a routine with one step list is a pipeline of one stage

column2: a fifth kind of module
column3: spec / sdk / core / plugins
column7: the module set and the import graph are fixed ("the arrows are the whole import graph")

column1: a competing owner of an existing word
column2: a second implementation of a registry key
column3: one provider per registry key
column7: a registry key has exactly one owner; a duplicate is a load error naming both
